$comment: Interop vectors for the E2EE record layer and the /open handshake (specs/end-to-end-encryption/NONCE-DESIGN.md §11, §12, §16). Every value is base64 unless the field name says base64url. A client reproduces each `frame` byte for byte from its `key`, `nonce`, `aad` and `plaintextUtf8`; `frame` is the 30-byte plaintext header followed by ciphertext‖tag, and on REST channels the AAD is that header plus the 32-byte target hash, which is NOT transmitted. Counters are strings because JSON has no 64-bit integer. The `negative` array is the half that matters: a client that matches only positive vectors can still accept a mutated AAD, a reflected direction or a counter gap. These keys are fixtures, not secrets — they are the same values noise-ikpsk1-vectors.json already publishes. Regenerate ONLY when the protocol deliberately changes, and change both repositories in the same breath.
aadLayout: version(1) || ctxId(16) || direction(4) || counter(8) || channel(1) = 30 bytes
restAadLayout: the same 30 bytes || sha256(method || "\n" || path || "\n" || query) = 62 bytes

encodings.$comment: NONCE-DESIGN §12. Two implementations pass their own fixtures and still fail here.
encodings.ctxId: 16 bytes, base64url, unpadded, 22 characters — the same spelling in X-TB-Ctx and JSON
encodings.ticket: 16 bytes, base64url, unpadded, 22 characters (no live ticket is published here)
encodings.X-TB-Seq: decimal string of the bigint counter
encodings.wsFrames: binary opcode; the client must set binaryType accordingly

records.name: websocket c2s, counter 2^32 (a counter above 32 bits)
rest request c2s, counter 0, bound to POST /api/sessions/A/input
rest request c2s, counter 3, bound to GET /api/sessions?limit=50
rest request c2s, counter 7, %2F in the path and an unsorted query (§4 canonicalization)

restResponse.$comment: A response echoes the counter of the request it answers (§13(a)); there is no second sender counter. At most one sealed response per accepted request counter — a request the window or the AEAD rejected gets a PLAINTEXT error and never a sealed body.

negative.$comment: Each entry MUST be rejected. `seal-failed` means the AEAD must not authenticate it; `sequence-violation` means it authenticates and is then refused by the counter rule — and note the order: authenticate FIRST, so an unauthentic frame is never reported as a sequence violation (§5 R2 ordering, §9).

base.name: the authentic frame every mutation below starts from
base.plaintextUtf8: the frame every negative vector mutates

cases.name: version byte flipped
cases.why: the AAD binds the envelope version

cases.name: ctxId re-pointed at another context
cases.why: the AAD binds ctxId; a receiver that owns THAT ctxId must still refuse it

cases.name: direction flipped to server→client
cases.why: the AAD and the nonce both bind direction

cases.name: counter renumbered to the expected slot
cases.why: the AAD and the nonce both bind the counter

cases.name: tag corrupted
cases.why: a frame nobody holding the key could have produced

cases.name: body truncated by one byte
cases.why: a short frame is refused, never padded or partially authenticated

cases.name: reflected: a server→client record fed back as client→server
cases.why: separate keys AND separate direction labels; a reflection must fail on both

cases.name: counter gap: an authentic frame at 5 while 4 is expected
cases.why: no window on the socket — a gap is a protocol violation, not a network event

cases.name: counter repeat: the base frame delivered twice
cases.why: a repeat is a replay; the second delivery must be refused

cases.name: rest request re-pointed at another session
cases.why: the 32-byte target suffix is the only thing binding a sealed body to its path

cases.name: rest request served under the percent-DECODED path
cases.why: §4: %2F is not a slash; decoding the path before hashing is the canonicalization mistake

open.$comment: The /open handshake (§11): psk-less IK, its own protocol name, its own prologue. A pairing message MUST fail against these — that is what the last field is for.

pairingMessage1RejectedHere.$comment: noise-ikpsk1-vectors.json's message1, which is a valid PAIRING message. Reading it with the /open prologue and no psk must FAIL. Without this vector, defaulting the prologue would silently remove the domain separation between the two handshakes.

restTargetCanonicalization.$comment: NONCE-DESIGN §4. The bytes hashed are the RAW wire request-target: method upper-cased, the percent-encoded path exactly as sent (never decoded, never normalised), and the query substring verbatim — original order, original `+` vs `%20`, duplicates kept. A client that decodes the path or re-serialises the query produces a different hash and every affected request fails to authenticate with only E2EE_SEAL_FAILED to debug it. Read it from the raw URL, never from a framework's decoded path.
